source_caption_text:
The way 40 flipped that Whitney sample needs to be studied

“Tuscan Leather” opens Drake’s 2013 album Nothing Was the Same with a six-minute track that takes its time and never relies on a traditional chorus. Produced primarily by longtime collaborator Noah “40” Shebib alongside Nathan Sessoms, the song is built around a three-part arrangement, with each section bringing a different sound and giving Drake room to switch up his delivery.

One of the most recognisable parts of the production is the way 40 flips Whitney Houston’s “I Have Nothing.” Instead of simply looping the sample, he changes its pitch and speed throughout the track, making it sound different in each section. The shifts give every verse its own feel while keeping the song connected from beginning to end.

That attention to detail is a big part of what makes “Tuscan Leather” stand out. Between the changing sample, the beat switches and the atmospheric production, 40 creates an instrumental that keeps evolving for the full six minutes. It also makes for a memorable opening to an album that remains one of Drake’s most celebrated projects.
